correctness.rationale: From the adjacency recurrence on the (q+1)-regular tree, resolvent F_r(A)=(1-r²)/(1+qr²-rA) has entries r^d; r d/dr and r²/2 d²/dr² give d r^d and binom(d,2)r^d, respectively. Read source N formula and independently used symbolic differentiation to verify N/D³ for arbitrary formal q,r,a,b, with degree <=2. The full adjacency spectrum and positive continuous spectral density justify pointwise N>=0 iff all finite-support quadratic forms PSD, and absence of spectral atoms at finitely many zeros justifies strict positive definiteness on finite distinct sites. Normalization ∫ N D^-3 dμ=1 and injectivity from d=1,2 give affine bijection onto all normalized quadratics. The extreme-point classification exhausts nonnegative quadratics with double internal or endpoint zeros, two endpoint simple zeros, and decomposable single-simple-edge zeros. Independent exact SymPy checks confirmed both q=4,r=1/4 rational notches: (285/164,225/164) yields 1215/41984 lambda²; (195/236,-225/236) yields 3375/60416(16-lambda²). No critical/supercritical r claim is made.

value.rationale: Motivated by natural polynomially weighted radial covariance families on regular trees; gives a complete, computable PSD parameter domain, exact extreme spectral notch designs and the distinction between vanishing continuous-frequency multipliers and finite-site Gram singularity. The full two-parameter extremal geometry is useful in covariance design and harmonic analysis rather than an unmotivated isolated instance.

final_claim: For q>=2 and 0<r<q^(-1/2), all homogeneous-tree covariances r^dist(1+a dist+b binom(dist,2)) are PSD exactly when their explicit quadratic numerator N_{a,b}(lambda) is nonnegative on the full adjacency band [-2sqrt(q),2sqrt(q)]. The normalized nonnegative quadratic cone is affinely isomorphic to the compact (a,b) body; its extreme points are the positive scalar squares (lambda-s)^2 for all s in the band and the sole two-edge polynomial 4q-lambda^2. Every admissible kernel is strictly PD on finite sets of distinct sites.
